A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Matching the relocated material supports a reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original representational-alignment measurements across networks, training checkpoints, distribution shifts, language models, and human brain responses, including Appendices A4–A8.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical analyses and additionally reports untrained-network comparisons and correlation/pixel-selection sensitivity checks.

M1.justification: The linear, Procrustes, and permutation/soft-matching framework, bidirectional averaging, and default center-pixel extraction remain. Spearman correlation and random-pixel sampling are supplementary evaluation checks; the PDFs do not establish a change to the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both retain ImageNet, CIFAR100, 17 OOD variants, STSB evaluation of Pile-trained Pythia models, and NSD brain data. Moving self-supervised, transformer, and language-model analyses into the main text adds no dataset or task. Omitted CIFAR100 transformer panels concern a model configuration within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 1 adds randomly initialized networks as comparators across layers under all three alignment metrics. v2 included epoch-zero networks in training analyses, but not this complete comparator set in the hierarchy comparison.

E3.justification: v3 adds protocols reporting Spearman rather than Pearson correlation after alignment (Appendix A2), selecting random rather than central feature-map pixels (A9), and comparing untrained controls. Existing training budgets and checkpoint schedules remain. The printed Spearman formula is incorrect, leaving its precise implementation unclear.

E4.justification: New targeted checks address correlation sensitivity to high-variance activations and sensitivity to spatial sampling. Existing rotation, OOD, and training-trajectory analyses largely remain, although the CIFAR100 ViT rotation panel disappears. Identical panels shared by new Figures A1 and A8 limit independent support for the two checks.

E5.justification: Both retain five-fold cross-validation, standard deviations across folds, OOD standard errors across 17 datasets, and brain-analysis variability across six participant pairs. No changed run counts, seed-reporting practices, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are established.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports trained-versus-untrained Procrustes increases of 145.26% in early layers and 493.84% in deeper layers, plus results described as stable under correlation and pixel-selection changes. CIFAR100 ViT hierarchy and rotation results from v2 Figure A5 are omitted. Most matched results, including the rotation-table values, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix A3 adds mathematical reasoning that nonnegative orthogonal matrices must be permutation matrices, connecting this property to ReLU basis alignment. v2 only reported the architectural contrast. The argument leaves implicit the stronger requirement of preserving the entire nonnegative orthant.

C1.justification: The abstract and key contributions retain the same three-axis audit and claims about near-linear Procrustes alignment, privileged CNN axes, early training convergence, and greater deep-layer divergence under distribution shifts.

C2.justification: Appendix A3 adds a proposed ReLU-versus-GeLU explanation for CNN/ViT differences in basis alignment. Appendices A2 and A9 interpret the added checks as supporting robustness to correlation and spatial-sampling choices. The principal discussion limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a public-code link and newly discloses MoCo batch size 256. Other training details are largely consolidated from v2. Conversely, Section 2 drops explicit linear-assignment/network-simplex solver descriptions and unequal-width Procrustes zero-padding instructions; these omissions do not establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds Braun, Grant, and Saxe's work on functional versus representational similarity in deep linear networks and removes Burkard et al.'s Assignment Problems reference. Appendix A3 expands discussion of already-cited privileged-axis research without substantially redefining the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: The method exposition is substantially compressed, former self-supervised/ViT/language-model appendices become Sections 4.4–4.6, CIFAR100 results are consolidated in Appendix A4, and training details are centralized. References move before the appendices. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: Figures and tables are extensively split, merged, resized, and relocated by dataset and analysis. v2 Figures 2–3 become v3 Figure 2 and Figure A3; Table 1 splits into ImageNet and CIFAR100 tables. Baseline and sensitivity overlays are added, and CIFAR100 ViT panels are removed.

improvement.justification: Untrained controls, code-access information, and targeted sensitivity checks offer useful additions. However, v3's Spearman formula omits ranks and squared differences, while Figures A1 and A8 reuse identical ResNet50, VGG16, and VGG19 panels for different tests, leaving the new evidence ambiguous. Some ViT results and solver/padding details also disappear. These benefits and reporting problems prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
